date_note: Date is the intrusion as reported by Dailysecu on 18 November 2026; the university learned of it on 17 November.
title: Jeonju University says its AHA education service was hacked, about 180,000 records leaked
summary: Dailysecu reports that Jeonju University's online liberal-arts education service "AHA" was hacked on 16 November, and the university noticed on 17 November. About 180,000 records leaked, about 25,000 of them including resident registration numbers; the article says records are not the same as people. The university halted the service and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission, KISA and the Ministry of Education.
plain: Jeonju University in South Korea says a hack of its online AHA education service leaked about 180,000 records, about 25,000 including resident registration numbers. It has told those affected.
exec: A university web service holding student, graduate and staff data was breached; check which small online services hold national ID numbers.
action: Jeonju University students, graduates and staff: watch for the university's SMS and email notice and be wary of messages that use your personal details.

validation.note: Only Dailysecu read, citing the university's notice and statement. Entry route not confirmed; no link to other university breaches confirmed (per the article).

review.note: Checked 16/17 Nov dates, about 180,000 records, about 25,000 with RRN, records-not-people caveat, reports to PIPC/KISA/MoE against Dailysecu
